gaps.term: Why updating D from H is linear-time but H from D is costly
gaps.quote: Both change only $D$, each combining $D$ with the earlier field $H$ in linear time.
gaps.note: The page asserts that the two updates of D are linear-cost while the middle update H<-H+D needs the network, but never says why the direction of the update (or H being the 'earlier' field) makes the difference, so the reader cannot check the cost split.

gaps.term: Cited bound s<Wm for the bit network
gaps.quote: For the bit network, $s<Wm$ (cited); the paper's proof computes $s$ as $Wm$ minus a positive constant fixed by the construction.
gaps.note: This inequality is the whole source of the speed-up, but the page never describes the bit network's calls or says what m is for it, nor how the construction removes calls; the cited claim stands in for how the page's own procedure works.
Unrolling Q_k <= (s/W)Q_{k-1}+C gives (s/W)^k Q_0 + C times the geometric sum; the minus sign does not follow from the recurrence, and the next sentences treat the sum as an added term.

gaps.quote: The geometric sum is also $O(m^{k\tau})$, since it is $O((s/W)^k)$.
gaps.note: A geometric sum of ratio s/W is O((s/W)^k) only when s/W>1; the page never establishes s/W>1 (only s/W<m), so the reader cannot check this bound.
The page never states m>=2, and the reader cannot see why m>=2 is needed for terms already shown to be O(m^{k tau}).
